proposed_core_edits.reason: The general finite-support model and every revalidated theorem require only two distinct support values. For \(L=2\), the mean-tangent map remains onto and the zero-mean shape tangent is the zero-dimensional space.

proposed.name: \(L\)
proposed.def: Known fixed number of outcome-support points.

prose_updates.tldr: A frozen menu of overlapping policies turns prospective randomized outcome annotation into a joint decision problem because one acquired treatment--stratum outcome informs several correlated policy contrasts. The kernel derives the conditional finite-coordinate LAN experiment uniformly over a saturated finite-support outcome model, including binary outcomes, and every contrast-preserving shape nuisance, characterizes the deterministic-design minimax regret value \(V^*\), gives certified computation on effectively represented inputs, and constructs a measurable nested-cell selector, joint AIPW estimator, and refined Gaussian rule attaining that value at tied, flat, disconnected, or dyadic-boundary design optima. The fully labelled pilot may diverge arbitrarily slowly provided its share vanishes: \(m_n\to\infty\) gives finite-cell moment consistency and \(m_n/n\to0\) makes its local information negligible. The selector's spatial convergence rate remains schedule- and law-specific through the positive prefix gaps. A generic continuous-objective witness shows only that continuity plus uniform objective approximation cannot yield an objective-uniform spatial recovery modulus; it is not a model-specific impossibility theorem for the Gaussian-risk family. An explicit \(L=3\) rational three-policy witness establishes that minimizing a scalar maximum pairwise-variance summary does not determine the Gaussian minimax-regret-optimal design: the unique optimizer of the pairwise-variance probe has regret above \(0.1965\), while a projected feasible competitor is below \(0.18453\), with separation on an explicit open neighborhood.

sampling_model.units: Independent main-wave records \(O=(X,A,R,Y^{\mathrm{obs}})\) have observed law \(\mathbb P^{\widehat r_n}_{p,q}\), where \(Y^{\mathrm{obs}}=Y\) if \(R=1\) and \(Y^{\mathrm{obs}}=\star\) otherwise, with fixed finite stratum space \([K]\), binary randomized treatment, and fixed known finite outcome support \(\mathcal Y\) of size \(L\ge2\), including binary outcomes.

project_justification.fill: The project fills the niche with a nuisance-uniform Gaussian experiment for fixed finite outcome support including binary outcomes, an exact deterministic-design minimax characterization, an effective certified solver, and a measurable tie-stable implementation requiring only \(m_n\to\infty\) and \(m_n/n\to0\). Its joint AIPW and Gaussian-rule construction attains the minimax value, while its spatial selector rate is stated honestly as schedule- and law-specific through the certified prefix-separation profile.

prose_updates.related_work: Hirano and Porter (2009) inform the scalar fixed-experiment Gaussian decision bridge, while Masten (2023) and Kato (2026) inform finite-action Gaussian games; none observes overlapping policy loadings through selectively annotated treatment--stratum cells. Higbee (2026) proves two-wave Bayes design under a unique, strongly concave smooth policy optimum. Theorem 4 gives the theorem-level contrast required here: the explicit \(L=3\) rational finite menu has a three-way tie in every local decision neighborhood and fourteen contrast-preserving selective-annotation nuisance coordinates, so Higbee's uniqueness and curvature conditions do not cover the experiment. Nwankwo, Goldkind, and Zhou (2026) supply the closest scalar annotation workflow, and the Wang, Wang, and Miao preprint, listed as a FUTURE Statistica Sinica article, supplies the nearest componentwise semiparametric two-phase criterion. Levis et al. (2024) inform observed-data influence projection, Cook, Mishler, and Ramdas (2024) inform stabilized AIPW limits, and Luedtke and van der Laan (2016) identify the nonregularity of nonunique optimal decisions. Those works do not establish the present coupling of a tie-stable multivariate regret design and a discontinuous finite-policy rule under only an arbitrarily slowly diverging pilot and a vanishing pilot share; the resulting spatial rate is deliberately schedule- and law-specific. Manski (2007) studies minimax-regret treatment choice when outcomes are missing for uncontrolled reasons and the response law is partially identified. Stoye (2007) extends incomplete-data choice to many treatments, and his finite-sample missing-outcome analysis studies a fixed exogenous missing fraction. Those decision problems are important antecedents but differ from prospective randomized annotation, known propensities, point-identified policy contrasts, and optimization of the acquisition design itself. Hu et al. (2024) inform regret-sensitive allocation in separable subgroup decisions. The auxiliary functional \(G_\omega\) is introduced internally only as the geometric probe in the constructive witness. Codi et al. (2025) provide the stacked rule-comparison consumer, and Kim et al. (2025) motivate independent validation of the azithromycin rules. The present general theory covers every fixed finite support with \(L\ge2\), including binary outcomes; continuous outcomes require a different support formulation.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The comparison class contains procedures whose fully labelled pilot sizes satisfy \(m_n\to\infty\) and \(m_n/n\to0\), and whose main-wave annotation rates converge to a deterministic feasible design; no polynomial pilot-growth condition is imposed. Fully sequential acquisition, positive-fraction pilots, bounded pilots, and random limiting designs are different experiments. The known fixed finite support has \(L\ge2\) distinct values and uniformly positive cell probabilities, so binary outcomes are included; continuous clinical outcomes require a separate support formulation. Certified computation is asserted only for rational-polytopal state sets and rational or real-algebraic encoded inputs with exact certificates; no algorithmic claim covers arbitrary opaque reals or oracle-free compact sets. The certificate returns value bounds and an outer minimizer cover, while the measurable selector has a schedule- and law-specific spatial rate determined by its pilot envelope and certified prefix gaps. The generic continuous-objective counterexample rules out a recovery modulus based only on continuity and uniform objective error; it does not establish a model-specific rate impossibility for the Gaussian-risk family. The auxiliary pairwise-variance functional \(G_\omega\) is used solely as the geometric probe in the explicit \(L=3\) witness. The \(M=2\) proposition recovers the known Blackwell-monotone variance benchmark; new geometry begins at three overlapping policies.
